body_html:
How to think about it

Objects are made of materials such as wood, glass, metal, plastic and cloth. Materials have properties: metals are lustrous (shiny), iron is hard and a sponge is soft, salt and sugar are soluble in water while sand and chalk are insoluble, and a cork floats while a stone sinks.

We can see clearly through transparent materials (glass), partly through translucent materials (butter paper) and not at all through opaque materials (wood). We group materials by these properties and choose the right one for each use.

Example

Can you see clearly through butter paper?

you can see a little

Answer: no: it is translucent

Example

Does chalk powder dissolve in water?

it settles

Answer: no: it is insoluble

Common mistakes

  • Calling translucent materials transparent.
  • Thinking all metals are soft.
  • Thinking heavy objects always sink.
